name: Ferrogrip Maglock Treader
description: A wide, flat-soled boot with an embedded magnetic locking plate in the forefoot and heel, designed for workers on elevated steel gantries and magnetized warehouse floors. The upper is stiff synthetic leather reinforced with a thin alloy toe cap. A rotary dial on the outer ankle adjusts magnetic pull between passive grip and active lock. Looks like a boot that was designed by someone who had never seen a boot — boxy, industrial, unmistakable.
functionality: Adjustable magnetic sole lock (passive grip to 80kg pull), steel-toe protection, anti-static lining
what_it_says: You work at height on industrial rigs or in automated warehouses. Safety is mandated, not chosen.
story_hooks: The maglock function can be remotely triggered — a saboteur who knows the frequency can lock a worker's feet to a gantry mid-shift.
Surplus units from a decommissioned Axiom contract show up on the Gray Zone markets, dials stripped out and resold cheap.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, utilitarian boot with an aggressively boxy silhouette. The toebox and heel are noticeably squared-off, and the sole is thick and perfectly flat—no heel-to-toe drop. The overall impression is of a tool rather than footwear: industrial, uncompromising, vaguely threatening.
physical_description.fit: Rigid and structured. The synthetic leather upper is stiff and unyielding, designed to support the leg rather than conform to it. Ankle support is firm without being binding. The sole is flat and wide, distributing weight evenly across a magnetized base.
physical_description.primary_material: Treated synthetic leather (ballistic-grade polymer composite) with embedded steel reinforcement panels and a ferrous-alloy toe cap. The sole is a magnetized compound composite with embedded iron-oxide particles.
physical_description.texture: Smooth synthetic leather with a faint industrial sheen. The toe cap has a brushed matte finish. The sole is slightly grippy to the touch, with barely-visible circular magnet housings flush with the surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray upper with charcoal reinforcement panels and a darker gray sole. The rotary dial on the ankle is brushed aluminum with a red indicator line.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty friction-fit laces with a reinforced toe box. No traditional buckles; instead, a locking collar around the ankle can be tightened via the rotary dial, which simultaneously adjusts magnetic engagement.
distinctive_features: Prominent rotary dial on outer ankle (brushed aluminum, red indicator mark)
Flush-mounted magnetic plates visible as faint circular indentations on forefoot and heel
Alloy toe cap with visible welded seams
Reinforced sidewalls with diagonal bracing panels
'AXIOM SAFETY WEAR' stamped into the heel in sans-serif caps
Subtle wear pattern on the inner ankle from repeated dial adjustment
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. Affordable industrial equipment for working-class substrate laborers, warehouse operatives, and gantry workers. Not luxury, not salvage—purely practical.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing these signals honest industrial labor. The wearer works in magnetized environments—steel mills, automated warehouses, elevated infrastructure maintenance. Marks someone as part of the essential substrate workforce keeping the GLMZ's physical infrastructure running.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically worn-in but not broken. The synthetic leather develops a patina of scuffs and micro-scratches. The sole shows faint wear marks where magnetic adherence is strongest. The dial rotates smoothly but may develop minor cosmetic scoring from repeated use.
